quests.instruction: Identify the nature place that is a cold forest full of tall, needle-leaved evergreen trees!
quests.question: Taiga
quests.hint: This cold, quiet forest stretches across the coldest parts of the world, just south of the tundra.
quests.explanation: Yes! Taiga is correct because it is a cold forest full of tall, needle-leaved evergreen trees.
quests.funFact: The taiga is the largest forest biome on Earth, stretching across huge parts of Russia and Canada!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature place that is a dry, treeless grassland found in cooler parts of the world!
quests.question: Steppe
quests.hint: This wide open land is drier and cooler than a warm savanna far to the south.
quests.explanation: Yes! A Steppe is correct because it is a dry, treeless grassland found in cooler parts of the world.
quests.funFact: The Eurasian Steppe is one of the largest grassland regions on the entire planet!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object that is a layer of soil that stays frozen solid all year long!
quests.question: Permafrost
quests.hint: Even in summer, digging down just a little reveals ground that never thaws.
quests.explanation: Yes! Permafrost is correct because it is a layer of soil that stays frozen solid all year long.
quests.funFact: Some permafrost has stayed frozen for tens of thousands of years without ever fully thawing!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object that is a piece of land surrounded by water on three sides!
quests.question: Peninsula
quests.hint: You could walk almost all the way around this land and see water on nearly every side.
quests.explanation: Yes! A Peninsula is correct because it is a piece of land surrounded by water on three sides.
quests.funFact: Florida is a famous example of a peninsula, with water almost completely surrounding it!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object that is a large group of islands scattered close together!
quests.question: Archipelago
quests.hint: A map of this area would show dozens, or even thousands, of small islands dotted across the sea.
quests.explanation: Yes! An Archipelago is correct because it is a large group of islands scattered close together.
quests.funFact: Indonesia is made up of an enormous archipelago of over seventeen thousand islands!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object that is a narrow strip of land connecting two much larger areas of land!
quests.question: Isthmus
quests.hint: Water touches both sides of this thin land bridge, squeezing it narrow in the middle.
quests.explanation: Yes! An Isthmus is correct because it is a narrow strip of land connecting two much larger areas.
quests.funFact: The Isthmus of Panama connects North America and South America, with an ocean on either side!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object that is a ring-shaped coral reef surrounding a calm lagoon!
quests.question: Atoll
quests.hint: From above, this ring of land and coral looks like a circle floating in the open ocean.
quests.explanation: Yes! An Atoll is correct because it is a ring-shaped coral reef surrounding a calm lagoon.
quests.funFact: Atolls often form around the edges of an old, sunken volcanic island!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object that is the natural home where a plant or animal lives and grows!
quests.question: Habitat
quests.hint: This is the specific place that gives a living thing exactly what it needs to survive.
quests.explanation: Yes! A Habitat is correct because it is the natural home where a plant or animal lives and grows.
quests.funFact: A polar bear's habitat is icy and cold, while a cactus's habitat is hot and dry!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object that is one of the seven huge landmasses making up the Earth's surface!
quests.question: Continent
quests.hint: This enormous piece of land is home to many different countries, mountains, and rivers.
quests.explanation: Yes! A Continent is correct because it is one of the seven huge landmasses making up Earth's surface.
quests.funFact: Africa, Asia, and Antarctica are just three of the seven continents on our planet!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature event where fallen leaves and old plants slowly break down into rich new soil!
quests.question: Decomposition
quests.hint: This slow, natural recycling process feeds nutrients back into the ground for new plants to use.
quests.explanation: Yes! Decomposition is correct because it is when fallen leaves and old plants break down into rich new soil.
quests.funFact: Without decomposition, fallen leaves would just pile up forever instead of feeding new plants!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature place covered in millions of pine and spruce trees that stay green all winter!
quests.question: Taiga
quests.hint: Winters here are long, dark, and bitterly cold, but the trees never lose their needles.
quests.explanation: That's right! Taiga is correct because it is covered in millions of pine and spruce trees that stay green all winter.
quests.funFact: Some parts of the taiga get so cold that it's one of the coldest inhabited places on Earth!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature place with short, tough grass stretching across a cool, dry, open plain!
quests.question: Steppe
quests.hint: Very few trees can survive the harsh winters found on this wide open plain.
quests.explanation: That's right! A Steppe is correct because short, tough grass stretches across its cool, dry, open plain.
quests.funFact: Ancient travelers once rode horses for months to cross the enormous open steppe!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object found just beneath the surface of the tundra, frozen no matter the season!
quests.question: Permafrost
quests.hint: This hidden, frozen ground keeps tall tree roots from ever growing deep in the tundra.
quests.explanation: That's right! Permafrost is correct because it lies frozen beneath the tundra, no matter the season.
quests.funFact: Scientists sometimes find perfectly preserved ancient plants and animals buried in old permafrost!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object that juts out into the sea, connected to the mainland by just one edge!
quests.question: Peninsula
quests.hint: This finger of land pokes out into the ocean, joined to the rest of the country by only one side.
quests.explanation: That's right! A Peninsula is correct because it juts into the sea, connected to the mainland by just one edge.
quests.funFact: Some peninsulas are so large that entire countries fit inside their borders!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object made up of many small islands stretched out across the ocean!
quests.question: Archipelago
quests.hint: Boats often travel between the many small islands that make up this scattered chain.
quests.explanation: That's right! An Archipelago is correct because it is made up of many small islands stretched across the ocean.
quests.funFact: Some archipelagos formed from a long chain of ancient underwater volcanoes!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object that acts like a thin land bridge between two bigger landmasses!
quests.question: Isthmus
quests.hint: This narrow strip could easily flood if the sea on either side rose even a little.
quests.explanation: That's right! An Isthmus is correct because it acts like a thin land bridge between two bigger landmasses.
quests.funFact: A famous canal was dug straight through an isthmus to let ships pass between two oceans!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object made of a circle of small coral islands with calm water in the middle!
quests.question: Atoll
quests.hint: Its ring shape protects the calm lagoon water from the rougher open ocean outside.
quests.explanation: That's right! An Atoll is correct because it is a circle of coral islands with calm water in the middle.
quests.funFact: Some atolls are barely a few feet above sea level, even though they stretch for miles!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object that provides food, water, and shelter for a living thing!
quests.question: Habitat
quests.hint: Every plant and animal is perfectly suited to live in its own particular kind of place.
quests.explanation: That's right! A Habitat is correct because it provides the food, water, and shelter a living thing needs.
quests.funFact: Protecting a habitat helps every plant and animal that depends on living there!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object so large that it contains entire deserts, forests, and mountain ranges within it!
quests.question: Continent
quests.hint: This massive area of land is measured in millions of square miles.
quests.explanation: That's right! A Continent is correct because it is so large it contains entire deserts, forests, and mountains.
quests.funFact: Millions of years ago, all of Earth's continents were joined together as one giant landmass!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature event that turns a fallen log into soft, crumbly soil over many years!
quests.question: Decomposition
quests.hint: Tiny helpers in the ground slowly break this old wood down, bit by bit.
quests.explanation: That's right! Decomposition is correct because it slowly turns a fallen log into soft, crumbly soil over years.
quests.funFact: A fallen tree can take many years to fully decompose back into the forest floor!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature place found just south of the frozen tundra, thick with evergreen forest!
quests.question: Taiga
quests.hint: This enormous forest circles much of the northern part of our planet.
quests.explanation: Great job! Taiga is correct because it is found just south of the tundra, thick with evergreen forest.
quests.funFact: The taiga is home to some of the toughest trees on Earth, built to survive freezing winters!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature place that stretches flat and dry between forests and true deserts!
quests.question: Steppe
quests.hint: This grassy plain gets just enough rain for grass to grow, but not enough for many trees.
quests.explanation: Great choice! A Steppe is correct because it stretches flat and dry between forests and true deserts.
quests.funFact: Wild horses have roamed the open steppe for thousands of years!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object that keeps the ground rock solid, even during a warm summer day!
quests.question: Permafrost
quests.hint: Only a thin top layer of this frozen ground ever thaws, even in the warmest months.
quests.explanation: Great job! Permafrost is correct because it keeps the ground rock solid, even on a warm summer day.
quests.funFact: As the Earth warms, some ancient permafrost is slowly beginning to thaw for the first time in ages!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object where the coastline wraps almost entirely around a strip of land!
quests.question: Peninsula
quests.hint: Nearly the whole outline of this landform touches the sea, except for one narrow connection.
quests.explanation: Great choice! A Peninsula is correct because the coastline wraps almost entirely around this strip of land.
quests.funFact: The word 'peninsula' comes from Latin words meaning 'almost an island'!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object that looks, from above, like a scattering of islands across the sea!
quests.question: Archipelago
quests.hint: From an airplane window, you might count dozens of these small islands below.
quests.explanation: Great job! An Archipelago is correct because from above, it looks like a scattering of islands across the sea.
quests.funFact: The Philippines and Japan are both well-known examples of a large archipelago!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object where land narrows down to a thin strip between two seas!
quests.question: Isthmus
quests.hint: Standing in the middle of this narrow strip, you might see water on both your left and your right.
quests.explanation: Great choice! An Isthmus is correct because land narrows to a thin strip between two seas here.
quests.funFact: Some countries exist entirely on a narrow isthmus connecting two much bigger continents!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object that forms a natural, circular barrier around a peaceful lagoon!
quests.question: Atoll
quests.hint: Palm trees often grow along the narrow strip of land that makes up this coral ring.
quests.explanation: Great job! An Atoll is correct because it forms a natural, circular barrier around a peaceful lagoon.
quests.funFact: The Maldives is a country made up almost entirely of beautiful coral atolls!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object that changes completely depending on which plant or animal calls it home!
quests.question: Habitat
quests.hint: A fish's watery home looks nothing like a squirrel's home high in a tree.
quests.explanation: Great choice! A Habitat is correct because it changes completely depending on which living thing calls it home.
quests.funFact: Losing its habitat is one of the biggest challenges any plant or animal can face!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object that is surrounded mostly by ocean and stretches across thousands of miles!
quests.question: Continent
quests.hint: Maps divide the whole world's land into just a few of these enormous pieces.
quests.explanation: Great job! A Continent is correct because it is surrounded mostly by ocean and stretches across thousands of miles.
quests.funFact: Continents are still slowly moving today, even though we can't feel it happening!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature event that recycles old plants back into nutrients the soil can use again!
quests.question: Decomposition
quests.hint: This natural process is nature's own quiet way of recycling everything it grows.
quests.explanation: Great choice! Decomposition is correct because it recycles old plants back into nutrients the soil can use.
quests.funFact: Decomposition is one of nature's best recycling systems, turning old plants into food for new ones!
